chunks.arabic_text: عَلِيّ بْنُ حَسَّانَ بْنِ كَثِيرٍ، مَوْلَى أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الْبَاقِرِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ)، أَبُو الْحَسَنِ. رَوَى عَنْ عَمِّهِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ. غَالٍ، ضَعِيفٌ. رَأَيْتُ لَهُ كِتَابًا سَمَّاهُ "تَفْسِيرُ الْبَاطِنِ" لَا يَتَعَلَّقُ مِنَ الْإِسْلَامِ بِسَبَبٍ. وَلَا يَرْوِي إِلَّا عَنْ عَمِّهِ. وَمِنْ أَصْحَابِنَا: عَلِيّ بْنُ حَسَّانَ الْوَاسِطِيُّ: ثِقَةٌ ثِقَةٌ.

translations.en: Ali ibn Hassan ibn Kathir, the client of Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him), Abu al-Hasan. He narrated from his uncle, Abd al-Rahman. A ghali ( exaggerator), weak. I saw that he has a book he called "Tafsir al-Batin" that has no connection to Islam by any means. He does not narrate except from his uncle. And from our companions: Ali ibn Hassan al-Wasiti: thiqa thiqa (highly trustworthy).

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Duʿafāʾ* highlights Ali ibn Ḥassān ibn Kathīr, a companion of Imam al-Baqir (AS), noting his status as a *ghalī* (proponent of extreme views) and weak narrator who relied exclusively on his uncle. The text distinguishes him from the trustworthy Ali ibn Ḥassān al-Wāsīṭī, while referencing his work *Tafsīr al-Bāṭin* to illustrate the early development of esoteric interpretation within Shia circles. This distinction is crucial for understanding the transmission of hadith and the criteria used by scholars to differentiate between similar-named narrators.
en.seo_question: Who is Ali ibn Hassan ibn Kathir and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالٍ: Ghali (one who exaggerates the virtues of the Imams, often to the point of deviance)
key_terms.تَفْسِيرُ الْبَاطِنِ: Tafsir al-Batin (Exegesis of the Inner/Hidden Meaning)
key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: Our companions (referring to the Shia jurists/companions of the Imams)
